covering.note: Its thick, woolly coat keeps it warm.

diet.note: Bamboo is almost all of its food.

activity.note: It is active about 14 hours a day.

young.note: A mother may have twins, but usually only one survives.

lifespan.note: Wild pandas live about 15 to 20 years; zoo pandas have reached 35.

clues.text: Its white coat has black ears, eye patches, legs and shoulders.
It has a 'false thumb', a wrist bone covered by a pad, that helps it hold bamboo.
It has a very strong bite, with big jaw muscles and wide, flat back teeth for crushing bamboo.
Bamboo makes up more than 99% of its food.
It feeds on the ground, but it is a good tree climber.
It rubs scent on tree trunks and rocks to mark its home area.
It lives high in the mountains, in cool forests with thick bamboo underneath.
It lives only in a few mountain ranges in central China.
A network of 67 nature reserves now protects about two thirds of wild pandas.

facts.text: A newborn cub is pink, blind and about the size of a stick of butter, around 1/900th of its mother's weight.
China's panda counts rose from 1,216 in the 1980s to 1,864 in 2011 to 2014, after poaching was banned and reserves were set up.
The name 'panda' first belonged to the red panda; the giant panda was named about 40 years later.
It eats up to 12.5 kg of bamboo a day, because it can digest only about a fifth of it.
Unlike most bears, it does not hibernate; in winter it shelters in caves and hollow trees.
A cub may stay with its mother for up to three years.
Every 15 to 100 years a whole bamboo species flowers and dies at once, which can leave pandas short of food.
Climate change could wipe out more than a third of its bamboo habitat in the next 80 years.
